what: Distance methods vs. the topology method
title: Getting Started with codiv
text: three default methods (Hommola, PACo, ParaFit) distance-based: correlate pairwise phylogenetic distances, sensitive branch lengths. Two trees branching order different evolutionary rates score less perfect match. optional "topology" method asks different question: two trees branching order?, ignoring branch lengths entirely. can flag congruence distance methods understate rates differ hosts symbionts. tree-shape comparison needs one tip per host, topology method reduces host largest single-host clade (tie-broken tightest branch lengths). host whose symbionts completely scattered coherent position excluded. Two diagnostic columns make visible: Topology_hosts_used — many hosts contributed node’s test Topology_fraction_kept — fraction symbiont tips retained reducing host dominant clade low Topology_fraction_kept means congruence rests heavy pruning; treat nodes caution, note nodes fewer three usable hosts return NA.
code: codiv_results <- codiv(   Host_tree = Host_Tree,   Symbiont_tree = Symbiont_Tree,   Host_to_Symbiont_df = Host_to_Symbiont,   methods = c("hommola", "topology"),   # topology is opt-in   permutations = 99 )

title: Getting Started with codiv
text: gauge false discoveries whole scan, codiv implements second-order permutation test: permute host tree’s tip labels, rerun entire scan, build null distribution number significant clades. appropriate approach nested clades tree independent, per-node multiple-testing correction (e.g. Benjamini-Hochberg) invalid . codiv_null_scans() : permutation reruns full scan, captures exactly dependence structure among nested clades. recommended way report significance scan.
code: null <- codiv_null_scans(   Host_tree = Host_Tree,   Symbiont_tree = Symbiont_Tree,   Host_to_Symbiont_df = Host_to_Symbiont,   n_permutations = 100,          # host-label permutations (outer null)   stat_threshold = 0.75,         # r > 0.75 ...   p_threshold = 0.01,            # ... and p < 0.01 define "co-diversifying"   permutations = 999, methods = "hommola", cores = 8 )  null$observed        # significant clades in the real data mean(null$null_counts)  # expected under permuted host labels null$global_pvalue   # is the scan more co-diversifying than chance? null$empirical_fdr   # expected false-discovery proportion at these thresholds

title: codiv 0.1.0
text: Initial release. codiv() scans qualifying internal node symbiont tree codiversification host tree using Hommola, PACo, ParaFit methods, plus opt-branch-length-free topology-congruence test. codiv_null_scans() provides scan-level (second-order permutation) false-discovery assessment respects non-independence nested clades. Secondary analyses: loo_host_analysis(), sensitivity_analysis(), host_codiv_summary(), molecular_clock(), filter_results(), plot_codiv_trees() tanglegrams. simulate_codiv_data() generates host/symbiont datasets known ground truth. Ships rodent gut-microbiome dataset Sprockett et al. (2025) inst/extdata.
